The unofficial GTA 6 PC port CGBJ posted a Windows launcher on 26 November and its GitHub repository now returns 404 for reasons unknown, with GitHub publishing no takedown notice naming it, while PortWatchVI relays a 25fps average in gameplay - Make Tech Easier
articles.chapeau: The unofficial GTA 6 PC port CGBJ posted a Windows launcher on 26 November and its GitHub repository now returns 404 for reasons unknown. PortWatchVI relays a 25fps average in gameplay and says it found no independent reproduction of that figure.
articles.txt:
Practical fixes for the tech you already own. Free, a few times a week.
The unofficial GTA 6 PC port CGBJ published a Windows x64 launcher and runtime in a public GitHub repository early on 26 November 2026. The repository and release page returned 404 on a later check. The cause is unknown. As of the GTA VI PC Race tracker’s check at 00:21 UTC on 27 November, GitHub had published no notice naming the repository. The tracker still relayed PortWatch’s reported average of 25 frames per second in gameplay, and PortWatchVI says it found no independent reproduction of that result and that the figure is not tied to the later public release.
According to the project history kept by PortWatchVI , CGBJ published the launcher and runtime at 06:35 UTC in a public GPL-3.0 repository. The release recorded the build and a checksum, and it required separately supplied game files. PortWatchVI says the cause of the 404 is unconfirmed. A pinned note on PortWatch describes the code as having been public and says it was taken down temporarily.
The GTA VI PC Race tracker logged the timing more closely. At 07:23 UTC PortWatch named a repository as CGBJ’s public code. That repository answered the tracker at 07:34 UTC. It did not answer at 08:01 or 08:03 UTC, while other repositories did. The tracker said the repository could be missing, private or removed. PortWatch moved CGBJ back to its list of private builds at 15:00 UTC, saying the code was offline.
XDA Developers reported that it was unclear whether the team made the project private to avoid a potential takedown notice or whether Rockstar’s legal department acted. XDA noted that GitHub DMCA takedown notices usually take at least a few days to become public. XDA also reported that several forks of the project were still active and said the team may have pulled the repository itself. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, previously used a DMCA takedown to remove the Leonida port as part of a network of 3,007 repositories.
PortWatchVI says the original PortWatch tracker reported a 25 fps gameplay average on an NVIDIA system with 16 GB of video memory and 8 GB of system RAM. PortWatchVI says the tracker gives no GPU model, test scene or run length. It also says the tracker does not tie that measurement to the later public release.
Notebookcheck, citing PortWatchVI , reported an average of 25 fps in gameplay and 30 fps in cutscenes. A later Notebookcheck article said those claims had yet to be independently verified. XDA also relayed the reported range of 25 to 30 fps. The Race tracker says press reports from 26 November relay unverified claims of 25 to 30 fps in the first boat mission. None of those reports gives a session length.
According to the Race tracker, CGBJ’s development journal shows medians of 54 to 58 milliseconds a frame, or about 17 to 18 fps. Those runs were in the opening street on an RTX 5090 with 32 GB of memory, around midnight UTC. Those were short harness runs of about two minutes, and the tracker reports no session of play.
The Race tracker says CGBJ forked VIctory-7900XTX, a version of VIctory, and added six commits of NVIDIA work. XDA says CGBJ uses a hybrid compatibility layer that combines VIctory’s runtime with shader translation from XCL. VIctory is still public. Its README on 25 November said the port was not playable yet because of the frame rate, at about 1 frame per second in the world. PortWatchVI lists a VIctory main-branch test on an RTX 5090 that reached 1.1 to 1.7 fps in the world and ended in a GPU hang roughly a minute in.
XDA reports that these ports are based on a leaked copy of the Xbox version of the game. Cyberleek released the Xbox executable on 23 November .
The Race tracker says VGTimes reported on 26 November that a packaged build attributed to CGBJ was circulating, a claim nobody has verified. The tracker also warns that downloads offered as GTA VI for PC have carried malware. Separately, NordVPN says a GTA 6 PC port scam kit was offered on the dark web for $200, payable in Bitcoin or Tether according to TechRadar and TechRepublic.
In its 26 November report, XDA said Rockstar had yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6. XDA cited rumors of a PC release six months to a year from the date of that report.

articles.chapeau: From GT to GTA
articles.txt:
Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6 .
Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist , says he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.
In a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he says he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”. He’s credited as a developer on the Physics Development Group, and he said in his video that the entire team was “amazing”.
The Edinburgh-based dev is no stranger to real-life racing, as it fielded its own winning team in the 24 Hours of Nürburgring event four years ago. Ben Lyons, who made up part of the squad, was the Technical Director in charge of physics on the title.
Each type has its own distinctive handling model, and you can really feel the difference when you go to a Mod Shop and tune your car to taste.
It doesn’t have the distinctive heavy handling of GTA 4 , but it’s also not quite as arcadey as GTA 5 either – I’d say it sits somewhere comfortably between the two, which is a good place to be.
I love all the extra work that’s been put into the DualSense’s haptic feedback, too; the way you can physically feel the change of grip between the different road surfaces – it’s impressive stuff.
I just wish Rockstar had put a little more energy into the races themselves, because they do rely on aggressive rubber banding, which is pretty frustrating. Considering how meticulously the rest of the game is crafted, it would have been nice if a bit more thought went into this aspect.
All in all, though, I’m not surprised to learn GTA 6 had real-life race car drivers and pro Gran Turismo players on its team. You spend a good chunk of your time in Leonida driving, and I think by and large Rockstar really nailed this important aspect of the game.

articles.t: Des fans font tourner GTA 6 sous Windows à 20 FPS, avec des chutes à 10 FPS en ville
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 tourne sur PC autour de 20 FPS dans une vidéo, mais chute à 10 FPS en ville. Matériel inconnu, bugs et retraits GitHub compliquent ces portages amateurs.
articles.txt:
Une balade en jet-ski sous Windows, puis un passage en ville qui fait tomber le compteur autour de dix images par seconde : la communauté avance, mais la fluidité ne suit pas encore. Ces premières séquences montrent surtout la distance entre un jeu qui démarre et un portage réellement jouable.
Rockstar n’a toujours communiqué aucun calendrier pour sa version PC de GTA 6. Des rumeurs évoquent le premier trimestre 2027 , tandis que plusieurs projets communautaires de recompilation et de portage progressent à partir de la version Xbox divulguée.
Publiée par AzRage sur X, une vidéo de deux minutes présente une version baptisée « CGBJ build », avec un compteur de performances visible. Celui-ci affiche 30 FPS dans les menus, puis oscille entre 19 et 23 FPS lors des déplacements en jet-ski ou en voiture le long de la côte. En ville, il descend aux alentours de 10 FPS.
Les défauts graphiques sautent également aux yeux : l’eau manque sur certaines portions du littoral et des traînées magenta recouvrent une route. La configuration utilisée n’est pas précisée, ce qui empêche de rapporter ces résultats à une puissance CPU ou GPU donnée, ou d’estimer la marge de progression.
Cette « CGBJ build » repose sur VIctory , un projet open source de recompilation permettant d’exécuter nativement sous Windows le code Xbox Series divulgué, avec des fichiers de jeu fournis par les utilisateurs. VIctory est actuellement présenté comme le projet le plus avancé de ces efforts communautaires, mais d’autres progressent et cette hiérarchie reste mouvante.
Les résultats annoncés par le fork public VIctory-NVIDIA donnent un autre point de comparaison : 20 à 22 FPS en moyenne dans les intérieurs du prologue, contre 24 à 31 FPS dans les zones moins chargées. Ce projet utilise le profil Xbox Series S et calcule l’image en 960 × 540 avant mise à l’échelle . Ces chiffres ne sont donc pas directement comparables à ceux de la vidéo CGBJ.
Ces travaux ont démarré après la diffusion en ligne de l’intégralité d’une build Xbox Series X par Cyberleek, qui a notamment lancé les efforts de recompilation autour de Leonida. Take-Two Interactive a depuis fait retirer Leonida ainsi que plus de 3 000 dépôts liés sur GitHub au moyen de notifications DMCA.
Le dépôt GitHub attribué à CGBJ est lui aussi devenu inaccessible le jour de la publication de la vidéo. La raison de cette disparition n’est toutefois pas connue : rien ne permet de l’attribuer à la même procédure.
Au-delà de cette build, les autres portages et recompilations observés souffrent encore de problèmes d’éclairage, de textures et d’ombres, auxquels s’ajoutent des bugs et une instabilité générale. Il reste donc beaucoup à corriger avant de proposer une expérience jouable dans de bonnes conditions, indépendamment du seul compteur de FPS.
Mieux vaut enfin éviter les téléchargements présentés comme des « portages PC de GTA 6 » : certains peuvent dissimuler des logiciels malveillants. Une vidéo montrant le jeu en fonctionnement ne garantit ni l’origine ni l’innocuité des fichiers proposés ailleurs.

articles.chapeau: Find all 20 Kitty Litter lab locations in GTA 6 with our complete guide. Discover every drug lab, the Balsero keypad code and how to unlock Spin On This…
articles.txt:
The Kitty Litter labs in GTA 6 are a series of hidden drug laboratories scattered across Vice City and its surrounding areas. Finding and destroying them is part of Jason’s side activities with Tyrone and Dook, but tracking down every location can be tricky.
If you’re struggling to find the laboratories, this guide covers all 20 mapped Kitty Litter lab locations in GTA 6, including directions to their entrances and tips for dealing with the guards protecting them.
Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub , featuring beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more.
To unlock the Kitty Litter activity, you’ll first need to complete the Chapter 3 story mission Here, Kitty Kitty.
After meeting Tyrone and Dook, you’ll be introduced to the drug laboratory operation and tasked with tracking down the locations around Vice City.
Look out for purple smoke coming from buildings, Spin On This laundry vans parked outside and purple cat graffiti. These are useful indicators that a Kitty Litter lab is nearby.
There are 20 mapped laboratory locations to discover. Here’s where to find them.
There are three Kitty Litter Labs outside of the Vice City area of the map, all thrree of which of which are in the are just to the right of the airport. Four more are across the river to Vice City west, with the remaining Kitty Litter Labs spread across the city itself.
While you can just use my map above to tick them all off, if you want specific details and zoomed-in map locations, check the list below.
Find the flats and head towards the second door on the top floor. The entrance is locked, so climb onto the green dumpster around the right-hand side and enter through the open window. You can also blow the door open with an explosive.
Look for the Spin On This laundry van beside the flats. Take the staircase on the right and enter the laboratory through the door at the top.
Head through the trailer park until you reach a parked car. Climb through the open window of the nearby white trailer to access the laboratory.
Find the two laundry vans in the parking area. Jump over the fence and head left through the gate. The laboratory is behind the shutter beside one of the vans.
Find the laundry van outside the flats. Take the staircase in the parking lot and head to the second floor. The laboratory is behind the white door furthest to the right.
Look for the laundry van beside the southern entrance to the plaza. Head upstairs and find flat 103, identified by the purple containers outside.
Find the laundry van parked outside the garage. The laboratory is behind the large shutter. You can open the shutter with the Slim Jim, or blow it up.
Head towards the tattoo parlour’s parking lot and locate the laundry van. The laboratory is behind the parlour, accessible through a brown shutter.
Find the laundry van beside the fence in the alley. Enter through the guarded gate and look for the laboratory to the left of the cat picture.
Look for the large garage gate beside the laundry van. Enter the keypad code 1999 to access the laboratory.
Find the laundry van beside the parking lot entrance. Take the staircase on the right and head upstairs to flat 5. The laboratory is behind the middle grey door. Look for the purple smoke
Look for the laundry van parked in the lot. Walk around the right-hand side of the building to find the laboratory behind a brown garage shutter.
Head towards Peterson’s Autoshop. Move the laundry van blocking the garage entrance to reveal the laboratory shutter.
Enter the trailer park through the double gates on the eastern side. Head towards the last trailer on the right. Be prepared to deal with the hostile occupants.
Find the laundry van and continue down the nearby alley. Look for the yellow garage shutters. The laboratory is behind the shutter beside the cat picture.
Locate the laundry van outside the houses. Walk around the side of the building and look for the white ground-floor entrance.
Enter the building where the laundry van is parked outside. Look for the second door on the left.
Enter through the green gate on the north-western side of the trailer park. Turn right, then left after passing the white van. Look for the green house with purple smoke coming from it.
Enter the parking lot through the southern entrance and make your way towards the garage shutter. Open it to access the laboratory.
Enter the trailer park through the south-eastern entrance

articles.chapeau: "Grand Theft Auto 6" has tons to do, but eventually you might like to see the ending. Or one of the endings, at least. We've got an overview to help you choose.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "GTA 6"
The map of "Grand Theft Auto VI" is huge and full of secrets , and Leonida offers amazing side activities that double as massive time sinks. Still, nothing lasts forever, and even the Bonnie and Clyde adventures of Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval will eventually reach their ending. But which ending will it be?
Many great video games have multiple endings , and "GTA VI" is no exception. In fact, players have already found at least six different endings, and it's entirely possible that others will turn up as people dig deeper into the hidden depths of the game.
The way the "GTA VI" endgame unfolds depends on important storyline decisions throughout the game, as well as your own actions during the finale. The amount of money on your BuckMe savings account, the strength of Lucia and Jason's relationship, and the status of the pair's criminal profiles are all contributing factors, too.
Rockstar Games Lucia and Jason's story comes to an end in the aptly titled mission "The End of the Road," which involves a massive attack at Giorgio Gallo's penthouse and a mad dash to safety along a police-infested highway. It's all very risky, and understandably, all of the endings lead to at least one protagonist dying or being incarcerated. Before we get to the truly depressing stuff, though, let's take a look at the nicer endings where both of Tomás' parents make it out of the game's main story alive.
All of the good endings require you to make it to a bridge with a police roadblock, where you must choose to "swim for it" (head toward the water with the intention of jumping in) instead of the "no surrender" option (charge at the roadblock). From that point on, it's all down to your past actions in the game.
The best ending in "GTA VI" requires low criminal profiles, at least $2.5 million on the BuckMe savings account, and a strong Hot Together relationship. Lucia and Jason also must kill Captain Aldo Méndez before the events of "The End of the Road." This way, Jason will take the fall for the pair's crimes. Lucia takes a deal with the government and remains free, and two years later, she's able to use the BuckMe money to bail Jason out. Finally together and free of trouble, Lucia and Jason get their happy ending and start building a new life with Tomás. If your criminal profile is low but you don't meet the other conditions, Jason still takes the fall — but remains in prison while Lucia and Tomás are seen visiting him.
Rockstar Games Lucia and Jason's story arc holds strong hints of impending tragedy throughout the game and many of the endings reflect that. The earliest one actually prevents you from playing the final mission at all: Should you spare Méndez and take his deal in the penultimate story mission "Protective Custody," Lucia and Jason are handcuffed and taken to a swamp, where we later see their bullet-riddled skulls next to a very happy-looking alligator.
Another early Méndez-themed exit happens if you take the deal but try to escape anyway. In this case, Jason will be shot by the police, and Lucia faces two bad choices. She can either die with the love of her life, or survive and end the game the same way she started it: A despairing petty criminal with no means of taking care of her son.
Choosing the "no surrender" option at the roadblock offers arguably the most cinematic "GTA VI" ending. It shows Lucia and Jason charging toward the roadblock and into the gunfire, still holding hands as they die. Even the "swim for it" option can lead to death — If your criminal profile is high enough, Jason will make the mistake of exiting the car with a gun in hand, at which point the cops will immediately open fire at the protagonists.
As mentioned, it's entirely possible that there are more "GTA VI" endings waiting to be discovered. Still, these six endings already give players plenty of reasons to replay those final hours. Not to mention, good cause to keep a few extra saves on hand.

The message was deleted shortly after it was posted, but not before it was widely noticed and called out for being a very bad idea.
"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," the message stated (via Kotaku ).
"The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!"
Lest there be any misunderstanding, a video that accompanied the post made the GTA 6 connection explicit: "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly. Performance seems to be the main issue for users wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to 'lock in and get your agents to help' if they need to."
And here's the accompanying video from @github's GTA6 tweet https://t.co/crU9cpOWcs November 26, 2026
The question of whether or not this sort of thing crosses a legal line has, predictably, sparked debate among those who think they have a clear understanding of the answer. What caught most by surprise, though, is that Github—which is owned by Microsoft—would put forth the question in the first place, implicitly suggesting that it might not. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive has been pretty aggressive with its efforts to keep recompiled versions of GTA 6 from landing on PC, and I can't imagine it would too thrilled with Github—which, I must emphasize, is owned by Microsoft —telling the world that it might actually be okay to go ahead and vibe-code it up.
That point wasn't missed by redditors, one of whom described it as Github " openly taunting Sony and Rockstar ." Even the AnyPS5 subreddit seemed baffled: Redditor superkickstart asked, "Do they have AI running their socials? Lol"
There's also a little bit of irony in the fact that, until earlier this week, the leading effort to get GTA 6 running on PC was based on an Xbox build of the game posted by GTA 6 leaker Cyberleeks. Beyond that, there are also some very obvious questions about how Github ( owned by Microsoft ) would react to AI-powered ports of, say, other software:
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
The whole thing is weird, really, because it seems like such an obviously bad idea. The only explanation I can come up with is that a social media manager either didn't think about it, didn't understand it (which would be weird in itself for someone doing social media posts for Github), or just had a big ol' brain fart. Whatever the reason, I imagine someone got a good old-fashioned talking-to about it.
I've reached out to Github and Take-Two for comment and will update if I receive a reply.

Take-Two’s (TTWO) GTA 6 Could Be a Cash Cow for the Next Decade TipRanks Thu, November 26, 2026 at 10:33 PM GMT+1 5 min read TTWO +2.36% DIS +2.80% Take-Two (TTWO) could have a cash cow for the next decade with Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6). The global video game publisher reported $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales for the title. Sam Houser, president of Take-Two's game developer Rockstar Games, called the release "a new chapter of Rockstar Games."
I think investors may still underestimate what that chapter could earn the company. The opening sales are extraordinary. An eventual PC release and online ecosystem could keep generating revenue long afterward. That prospect leaves me Bullish on TTWO stock.
An extraordinary launch sets up a strong Fiscal Q3 for Take-Two. Rockstar reported 32.5 million units sold before release. Beyond the anticipation and hype, the game seems to be an extraordinary artistic achievement for the industry. Its Metacritic critic score was 99. Morgan Stanley (MS) said the launch exceeded already high expectations.
For perspective, GTA 5's 2013 debut generated more than $800 million. GTA 6's opening was roughly 4.7 times that figure at $3.79 billion. Even Disney's (DIS) Avengers: Endgame's global opening weekend reached $1.209 billion. The formats differ, but the scale of spending is remarkable.
I believe GTA 6 could become a generational benchmark. Game Informer's review describes how small everyday encounters fit around elaborate criminal missions. The achievement appears to be coherence across an enormous, detailed world. I think we'll still discuss how Rockstar accomplished that many years from now.
Few studios could fund such a project for over a decade. They would still need Rockstar's technical skill and creative leadership. That makes this franchise exceptionally difficult to replicate.
The December-quarter earnings report should begin revealing the financial payoff. Management previously guided to $3.35–$3.50 billion of quarterly net bookings and $8.0–$8.2 billion for Fiscal 2027. Note that retail receipts are consumer spending. Bookings measure Take-Two's net product and service sales. So GAAP revenue recognition can follow a different timetable.
Even allowing for those differences, I think year-end holiday demand creates room for higher guidance. I want to see updated unit figures and premium-edition adoption. Management's roadmap for monetizing the installed player base will matter beyond the initial sales beat.
My thesis here is that a decade of exceptional sales figures could follow as Rockstar reaches new audiences. GTA 6 currently runs only on PlayStation 5 (PS5) and Xbox Series X/S. An eventual PC version could spark another substantial sales wave.
Also, future console versions could extend that further. Lower-priced editions would reach players who skipped the launch, while word of mouth can keep bringing people into a world worth exploring. GTA 5 has already demonstrated how long that process can last.
Take-Two now reports nearly 235 million units shipped for GTA 5 . GTA Online continues generating revenue more than 13 years after the original release. It's reasonable to assume that GTA 6's future multiplayer experience could surpass that precedent over its lifetime. It starts with an enormous potential audience and a much richer world. Virtual currency can monetize customization, while subscriptions can support more consistent spending. GTA+ already offers GTA 6 benefits.
Community-created content could keep players engaged between Rockstar's own updates. An online launch date remains unannounced, but its commercial potential looks substantial to me.
Paid story DLC could add revenue too, although Rockstar has confirmed no expansion. Take-Two also has BioShock and Judas in its pipeline. Meanwhile, National Basketball Association (NBA) 2K and World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) provide established franchises outside GTA. Zynga's upcoming mobile releases include CSR 3 and Top Goal.
These businesses give the company other ways to grow as GTA 6 moves beyond launch. I see the initial purchase as the beginning of a potentially much longer customer relationship.
Consensus may underestimate the long run if GTA 6 monetizes well. TTWO trades at 29.73x Fiscal 2027 earnings, falling to 22x Fiscal 2028 earnings. articles.t: GTA 6: UFO Walkthrough & How to Find Aliens
articles.chapeau: Look to the skies
articles.txt:
Are you looking for UFOs in GTA 6 ? Do you believe we're not alone in the universe? Well, you've come to the right place. In this GTA 6 guide , we've got information on how to find a UFO and unlock the The Truth Is Out There Trophy.
This guide will show you how to start the UFO mission in GTA 6 — and hopefully help you make contact with beings from another world. It all begins with finding Bud , who should show up once you reach Chapter 2 in the main story.
Your search for a UFO begins by tracking down a strange man named Bud , who can be found in random, secluded spots around Port Gellhorn — and only at night.
It doesn't matter if you're playing as Jason or Lucia — but as far as we can tell, you do need to be on your own.
When you do stumble across Bud , he's easy to spot because he'll be standing on top of his car, shouting into the sky:
You can tell it's him by pressing R3 + L3 and activating slow motion to see his noise marker.
Apparently, Bud can appear across the region in one of multiple locations — but he always seems to be close to a dirt road. We've ran into him not once, but twice on a specific beach — so you're probably best off looking there.
At the very least, it's worth driving near the coastline if you're struggling to find Bud . There are very few light sources out there, and so spotting the lights on Bud's car is fairly easy.
The beach where we found Bud is near the south of Kelly County , at around 8:30pm. Again, the sun needs to be down before Bud appears.
Talk with Bud and you'll spark up a conversation about his interest in extraterrestrials. Keep talking with him and you'll eventually be given the option of telling him he should probably wrap up for the night.
Bud will take the advice, thank you for your company, and drive off. He tells you that you can have the beers he left behind — but you don't need to drink them to continue this adventure.
Once you've talked with Bud , get back in your car and drive towards the woods around central Gellhorn at night. You can do this on the same night that you meet Bud .
You're basically looking for old dirt roads with very little to no traffic on them. They circle through and around the dense woods in the middle of Gellhorn's countryside.
This is where things can start to get weird. As you're driving, you may notice oddities like your radio cutting in and out. If you do, that means you're close.
Stick to the dirt roads in and around the Gellhorn woods and you may eventually come across an abandoned car just off the road, pointing into the woods. Your vehicle's radio should cut out completely as you get closer:
Exit your vehicle and take a look around — you'll notice that there are a bunch of clothes scattered across the ground, leading into the woods.
Follow the trail of clothes (take your torch out if you need the light) and you'll end up deep in the woods. Just keep going straight ahead.
After witnessing the impossible, talk to the naked stranger and ask if she needs help. She'll request that you go and get her car — the abandoned one back on the road.

articles.t: After removing GTA 6 PC ports, GitHub celebrates app popular in PS5 piracy groups
articles.chapeau: GitHub celebrated AnyPS5, a program that supporters hope will produce a GTA 6 PC solution. The deleted social media post is under scrutiny, since the resource removed 3,000+ other repositories related to the PS5 game. Prompted by promising unofficial ports, Take-Two issued DMCA takedown notices.
articles.txt:
On social media, GitHub noted how the GTA 6 release date encouraged an explosion of open-source projects. The platform highlighted AnyPS5 , an app that brings unofficial ports of PS5 games to PCs. However, it blocked similar efforts days earlier after a DMCA request from Take-Two . Critics are calling the now-deleted post hypocritical.
AnyPS5 is not a PS5 emulator in the traditional sense. Instead, the program focuses on making PlayStation titles run natively on Windows and Linux. The process involves converting eboot.bin files to compatible executables . Having obvious appeal to console-locked targets, it has accumulated 58,000 GitHub stars since its August debut.
In addition to the post, the platform uploaded a video promoting the app. Both raised the question, “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” That’s controversial, as Take-Two believes an open-source GTA 6 PC version constitutes piracy and infringes on copyrights.
The publisher confirmed that viewpoint by seeking a DMCA takedown of more than 2,900 GitHub projects. As a result, over 3,000 repositories vanished, including Leonida. The initiative capitalized on a full Xbox build distributed by Cyberleek. Because the Microsoft console and Windows share similarities, it made some progress prior to the shutdown.
PlayStation piracy and homebrew communities have been encouraged by the developments. At the same time, the PS5 jailbreak has advanced through various exploits. Most recently, a decrypted GTA 6 PS5 game dump surfaced, which is now running on consoles with older firmware. Even without owning the game, players can download and install files and explore Vice City .
Followers are asking why GitHub agreed to remove some repositories, while others with the same goal remain accessible. Praising AnyPS5's efforts to create a GTA 6 PC port only adds to the confusion.
Regardless of how many DMCA takedowns Take-Two pursues, it faces attacks from multiple fronts. Developers are rapidly optimizing performance on PCs even before Rockstar announces a retail Windows version.

Selon les données publiées, la version présentée utilisait environ 40 Go de mémoire vive. Le moddeur Bl4Ck0uuT a, de son côté, obtenu environ 27 fps et travaille à réduire la consommation de RAM avant de publier le code.

articles.txt:
D’après le dataminer Tex2, qui a fouillé les fichiers du jeu, et le site MP1st qui a relayé sa liste ce mercredi 25 novembre, la PS5 et la Xbox Series X utiliseraient les mêmes réglages, surtout en « moyen » et « élevé ». La PS5 Pro ajoute des ombres calculées en ray tracing, ce que Rockstar a confirmé, tandis que la Xbox Series S baisserait la qualité des textures et réduirait même la foule dans les rues. Nous avons détaillé cette fuite ici . Rockstar n’a pas commenté le reste de la liste.
Pour un PC, la conséquence est simple : les cartes graphiques de notre guide de configuration visent ces réglages de console. Pour jouer avec une image plus belle que sur PS5, il faudra davantage de puissance.
Pour l’instant, GTA 6 n’existe que sur PS5 et Xbox Series, où il est sorti le 19 novembre. Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune version PC, mais GamesBeat affirme, sur la foi de quatre sources anonymes, qu’elle est prévue pour le premier trimestre 2027 ; le studio n’a pas commenté. Ce serait bien plus rapide que pour GTA 5 , arrivé sur PC en avril 2015, soit environ un an et sept mois après sa sortie sur PS3 et Xbox 360.
L’information la plus solide vient de Digital Foundry , qui a comparé le jeu sur les quatre consoles. Toutes utilisent le ray tracing, une technique qui simule le trajet de la lumière, pour l’éclairage et les reflets. Même la Xbox Series S, la moins puissante , le conserve, quitte à calculer son image en 720p et à passer souvent sous les 30 images par seconde.
Aucune console ne permet de couper le ray tracing. Cela ne dit pas encore ce que proposera la version PC.
C’est un problème pour les PC équipés d’une carte sans circuits dédiés au ray tracing : GeForce GTX (séries 900, 10 et 16), Radeon RX 500 et RX 5000. Elles représentent encore plus de 13 % des PC du sondage Steam d’octobre 2026 . Certaines GTX savent faire du ray tracing grâce à leur pilote, sans circuits dédiés, mais rien ne garantit qu’elles seraient acceptées par GTA 6, ni assez rapides.
Je passe chez Apple ! Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Trois scénarios sont possibles, sans qu’on sache lequel Rockstar choisira.
Des circuits de ray tracing obligatoires. Ces cartes seraient alors exclues. C’est le choix d’ Indiana Jones et le Cercle ancien et de Doom: The Dark Ages , qui exigent une carte équipée pour le ray tracing.
Un ray tracing logiciel. Comme dans Star Wars Outlaws ou Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora , le jeu calcule alors le ray tracing sans circuits dédiés, et se lance donc sur ces cartes. Dans les tests de TechPowerUp en 1080p, une Radeon RX 5700 XT y fait jeu égal avec une RX 6600, équipée pour le ray tracing, alors qu’elle la devance d’environ 10 % dans les jeux sans ray tracing.
Un mode PC sans ray tracing. Rockstar l’a fait pour GTA 5 Enhanced, la version modernisée de GTA 5 sur PC : le ray tracing y est facultatif, et une GeForce GTX 1630 suffit au minimum.
Si un tel mode existait, le gain pourrait être important. Dans un test de GTA 5 Enhanced réalisé par le site polonais PurePC , activer le ray tracing fait perdre de 41 à 57 % des images par seconde en 1080p sur ces cartes courantes :
Sur 36 jeux testés en 4K, TechSpot mesure une perte moyenne plus modérée : de 22 à 32 % sur une GeForce RTX 4090, de 29 à 42 % sur une Radeon RX 7900 XTX, selon le niveau de ray tracing.
Ces mesures restent à prendre avec précaution, car GTA 5 est un jeu de 2013 auquel le ray tracing a été ajouté après coup, et PurePC ne l’a testé que sur une seule scène. Elles ne disent pas ce que gagnerait GTA 6 .
Digital Foundry juge d’ailleurs l’éclairage en ray tracing de GTA 5 Enhanced relativement léger pour la carte graphique, mais lourd pour le processeur. Enfin, notre guide suppose le ray tracing activé, comme sur console : ces gains ne s’appliquent pas à ses recommandations.
Avec les calculs de notre dossier , voici ce que donneraient des réglages au plus bas sur trois cartes graphiques très répandues. Ces projections reposent sur des gains mesurés dans d’autres jeux, souvent sur des cartes haut de gamme : ce ne sont que des ordres de grandeur.
En « bas », avec le ray tracing. Dans Red Dead Redemption 2 , du même moteur, ces réglages rapportent environ 13 à 26 % d’images par seco

And not just gamers who may be planning to run such an (illegal) unofficial port, but also those thinking about what the system requirements may be for Rockstar's official PC release.
The key info here comes from the 'CGBJ' build which has shared footage of GTA 6 running at a stable 25 to 30fps on PC as I reported earlier today . This port is currently hitting that frame rate on a PC with 8GB of system RAM and an Nvidia GPU that has 16GB of video memory (VRAM), and it's the latter point which is causing some concern.
Brackz on X , who highlighted this progress with the CGBJ project, asked their followers: "Seems like we might be seeing complete builds this weekend, will you be playing?"
And while some gamers do want to play — regardless of any risks associated with an illegal port, and that includes the danger of downloading a fake PC version that's malware in disguise, which are already around incidentally — they're quite worried about that 16GB of VRAM figure. Not many folks have a graphics card with this much memory on board, after all.
Is this really a concern, though – and more broadly, is it any kind of ominous sign for those planning to buy the official version of GTA 6 when Rockstar makes it available?
Well, I certainly wouldn't get carried away with the notion that seeing 16GB of VRAM mentioned in an unofficial port should be any cause for panic at this stage. articles.chapeau: What is on the encrypted hard drive in GTA 6? A senator, partial footage and a lot of unconfirmed claims. Here is what reports back up.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Spoiler warning: this article discusses a story item and a scene from Grand Theft Auto VI . If you want to find it yourself, stop here.
The encrypted hard drive is a story item in Grand Theft Auto VI , and players have spent days trying to work out what it holds. Beebom’s spoiler piece, which asked what is on the drive and claimed to answer it, became the top gaming story of the week. The honest answer is narrower than the headline suggests. The game decrypts part of the drive and shows footage of a woman referred to as “Senator.” It never shows the whole thing.
That gap between what the game shows and what the internet claims is the real story. Since GTA 6 reached PS5 and Xbox , players have pulled every thread in Leonida, and the encrypted drive is one of the loudest. This analysis separates what reports confirm from what they only suggest, explains why Rockstar might have built the scene this way, and lays out what to watch next.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with the basics. The encrypted hard drive is a story item inside the game, and reports place it in a bag alongside a statue. That is the full extent of what the fact record says about where it sits. Nothing in the coverage I reviewed gives a mission name, a map location or a sequence number, so this article does not invent one.
Why does a bag with a statue matter? Because it frames the drive as something a character wanted hidden or moved. A drive tucked in with a statue reads as cargo, not as a keepsake. That framing is analysis, not confirmed lore, and it should stay labeled that way. What reports do confirm is the pairing itself and the fact that the drive is encrypted.
Encryption is the key design signal here. A locked drive promises a payoff, and the game follows through by decrypting some of it. Players then see the result on screen, which is why the story spread so fast. The reveal is visual, short on explanation and heavy on implication.
The game shows decrypted video footage involving a woman referred to as “Senator.” Reports agree the footage includes the senator using drugs. That is the confirmed visual content, and it is the only content the reporting supports. Everything else attached to this scene needs a caveat.
The second confirmed point matters just as much. The footage is only a partial decryption. The game does not reveal the full contents of the drive, and reports say so directly. A player who watches the scene and walks away believing they have seen everything has misread it.
Think of it as a trailer for a document. The decrypted slice proves the drive holds compromising material and tells you who the material concerns. It does not tell you why the drive exists, who made it, or who wants it. Those gaps are where the speculation lives.
Several reports identify Camila Fuentes as the senator in the footage. That identification is itself confirmed as a pattern of reporting. Whether Fuentes is truly the woman on screen is a different question, and it stays unconfirmed. The coverage is inconsistent, and no official Rockstar source backs the match.
This distinction trips up a lot of readers. “Several outlets say X” and “X is true” are separate claims. When outlets copy each other, repetition looks like corroboration even though it is one source echoed five times. Treat the Fuentes name as a strong lead from players and writers, not as a character sheet from Rockstar.
The cautious reading holds up well. The game calls the woman “Senator,” which is a title, not a name. A name attached to that title in reporting could come from other scenes, dialogue or in-game documents that outlets stitched together. Without the underlying source, nobody can verify the link from the outside.
The unconfirmed list is longer than the confirmed one, and that is by design. Below is the clean split, built only from the fact record.
One report says the drive contains footage of Fuentes calling an unknown man “daddy” or “papi.” No other verified source repeats it. Treat it as a rumor until someone shows the scene with timestamps, or until Rockstar confirms it. It may be accurate. The point is that nobody has demonstrated it.

En quelques jours, des fans ont lancé une version pirate de GTA 6 sur PC à partir d’une fuite Xbox, alors que seul le jeu console est sorti. Ce coup de force inédit ouvre un bras de fer explosif avec Rockstar, dont l’issue reste très incertaine.
Grand Theft Auto VI est officiellement sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S , sans aucune date PC confirmée. Pourtant, quelques jours ont suffi pour que des développeurs passionnés fassent démarrer une version pirate de GTA 6 sur Windows à partir d’une build Xbox de 209 Go, complétée par un exécutable de 57 Mo publié par le groupe Cyberleek , comme le rappellent Les Numériques. Du jamais vu à cette vitesse.
Autour de projets comme Leonida , VIctory ou XCL , la communauté s’est fixé un objectif résumé par GameStar : avoir « GTA 6 pour PC avant GTA 6 pour PC ». Serveurs Discord géants, centaines de forks sur GitHub, outils d’IA pour aider au portage, tout s’est emballé en quelques heures. Reste à savoir si ce tour de force doit vraiment inquiéter Rockstar Games ou si l’éditeur peut, pour l’instant, dormir tranquille.
La base de tout, c’est la fuite de la version Xbox de GTA 6 , incluant les données complètes et l’exécutable. Les projets non officiels utilisent soit une recompilation statique, comme Leonida, qui traduit le binaire Xbox en binaire Windows, soit une couche de compatibilité comme XCL qui simule l’environnement de la console. Des outils d’IA servent à analyser le code et générer des portions compatibles PC plus vite qu’à la main.
Résultat concret : XCL affiche déjà les menus de GTA 6 à environ 30 images par seconde, en avalant près de 15 Go de RAM. VIctory va plus loin en chargeant le monde ouvert en une cinquantaine de secondes, mais la scène reste quasi noire et tourne à quelques fps seulement. Certains forks rapportent 22 fps pendant une quarantaine de minutes avant un crash de la carte graphique.
Leonida, lui, affirmait avoir converti tous les shaders et promettait une version jouable en « au moins une semaine » avant de disparaître. Malgré cette avancée, on est encore loin d’un jeu réellement praticable : pas de stabilité, pas de GTA Online , accès réservé à une poignée d’utilisateurs capables de manipuler une fuite illégale de plus de 200 Go.
Pour les joueurs PC, ces démonstrations prouvent surtout que GTA 6 tourne déjà, d’une façon ou d’une autre, sur leur plateforme alors que Take Two Interactive n’a toujours pas annoncé de version Windows. Comme pour GTA V et Red Dead Redemption 2 , la stratégie semble rester console d’abord, PC plus tard, des sources de l’industrie évoquant seulement un créneau autour du premier trimestre 2027.
En parallèle, les médias français alertent sur la prolifération de faux « GTA 6 PC » truffés de malwares. Télécharger une version piratée expose à des chevaux de Troie, mais aussi à des risques juridiques bien réels : en France, la contrefaçon d’une œuvre protégée peut entraîner jusqu’à 3 ans de prison et 300 000 € d’amende, même si l’ARCOM est moins visible qu’à l’époque de la Hadopi.
Pour jouer légalement sur un PC aujourd’hui, la seule voie reste le streaming depuis une console via Remote Play ou équivalent Xbox, avec un exemplaire acheté de manière classique. Tout le reste, qu’il s’agisse de builds compilées à partir de la fuite ou de faux installateurs, reste à éviter.
La réaction de Take Two a été immédiate. Le 24 novembre 2026, une plainte DMCA a conduit GitHub à retirer Leonida et 3 007 dépôts associés. Le serveur Discord du projet, qui avait atteint environ 179 000 membres, a été fermé, tout comme le compte du développeur principal, âgé de 15 ans, selon Frandroid. GameStar parle d’un « jeu du chat et de la souris » à une échelle inédite.
Sur le plan commercial, l’impact semble pourtant limité à court terme. Les versions actuelles sont instables, techniquement hors de portée du grand public et totalement privées de composante en ligne. Les quelques milliers de curieux capables de les lancer sont, pour la plupart, le cœur de cible qui achètera aussi la version officielle console ou PC.
Le vrai risque pour Rockstar se situe plutôt du côté de l’image et du contrôle de son jeu phare. Voir circuler des séquences illisibles à 5 fps sous l’étiquette « GTA 6 PC » brouille le message et met en lumière une faille de sécurité majeure. Mais cette agitation entretient aussi une visibilité énorme autour de GTA 6 et confirme l’appétit du public pour un portage Windows. Tant que Rockstar garde la main sur la version définiti

articles.chapeau: Une fuite des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 détaille plein de petits détails techniques sur les versions du jeu comme les ombres en ray tracing de la PS5 Pro. Sur Xbox Series S, les compromis iraient même jusqu’à réduire le trafic et le nombre de piétons dans Vice City.
articles.txt:
Une fuite des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 détaille plein de petits détails techniques sur les versions du jeu comme les ombres en ray tracing de la PS5 Pro. Sur Xbox Series S, les compromis iraient même jusqu’à réduire le trafic et le nombre de piétons dans Vice City.
Si toutes les versions de GTA 6 tournent à 30 images par seconde, la qualité des graphismes varie d'une console à l'autre. ©RichieSanders x Shutterstock Les différences entre les versions console de GTA 6 se verraient jusque dans les embouteillages de Vice City. Rockstar vise 30 images par seconde sur les quatre machines, et un relevé de réglages que le dataminer Tex2 dit avoir tiré des fichiers du jeu donne un aperçu des compromis faits pour tenir cette cadence.
Partagé le 25 novembre sur X par Tex2, le document a depuis disparu du réseau social. Heureusement, certains sites comme MP1st, ont pu reproduire les tableaux des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 , console par console.
Dans ces tableaux, la PS5 standard et la Xbox Series X partagent les mêmes réglages graphiques. Les textures et la tessellation, qui subdivise les surfaces pour affiner leur géométrie, y sont réglées sur « élevé ». L’illumination globale, le calcul des rebonds de la lumière entre les surfaces, reste sur « moyen ». Rockstar avait déjà précisé que les deux consoles calculent leur image en 1440p avant de la reconstruire en 4K avec le même algorithme maison d’anticrénelage temporel, ou TAA.
La PS5 Pro conserve les textures en qualité élevée et part elle aussi du 1440p. Elle s’appuie sur le PSSR 2 de Sony pour reconstruire l’image en 4K. Rockstar avait déjà confirmé qu’elle serait la seule à calculer des ombres en ray tracing .
D’après le relevé, l’illumination globale passerait sur « élevé ». Le lancer de rayons servirait à calculer l’ombre d’un arbre au soleil aussi bien que celle d’un passant sous un lampadaire. Les réglages correspondants, pour les ombres directionnelles et les ombres liées aux sources de lumière locales, seraient tous deux sur « élevé ». Leurs équivalents calculés par rastérisation passeraient sur « faible ».
Sur Series S, Rockstar part d’une image en 720p que le FSR 4 d’AMD reconstruit en 1080p. Les développeurs disent avoir tenu à conserver l’illumination globale en ray tracing malgré la mémoire plus limitée de la console. D’après les tableaux, la qualité des textures et celle de la simulation de l’eau et des vagues reculeraient à « moyen ». La tessellation, elle, tomberait sur « faible ».
L’écart se verrait aussi dans la rue. Sur Series S, la densité des piétons et celle du trafic seraient toutes deux réglées sur « moyen », contre « élevé » sur les trois autres consoles. Le même écart apparaît dans les réglages de la physique et dans plusieurs paramètres de l’IA. Comme quoi, même à Vice City, le diable se cache dans les détails.
GTA VI 79,99 € Foire aux questions Contenu généré par l’IA Quelle est la différence entre la rastérisation et le ray tracing pour calculer les ombres dans un jeu ? La rastérisation calcule l’image en projetant des triangles sur l’écran, puis en appliquant des astuces (shadow maps, filtrage, biais) pour simuler les ombres à moindre coût. Le ray tracing, lui, lance des rayons dans la scène pour déterminer si un point est éclairé ou occulté, ce qui produit des ombres généralement plus cohérentes (contacts plus crédibles, pénombres mieux gérées). En pratique, le ray tracing est nettement plus gourmand en calcul et en bande passante mémoire, d’où des choix ciblés (activer certaines ombres RT et baisser d’autres réglages). Beaucoup de jeux combinent les deux : RT pour quelques effets « premium », rastérisation pour le reste afin de tenir une cadence stable.
L’upscaling reconstruit une image de sortie (1080p/4K) à partir d’un rendu interne plus bas (720p/1440p) pour réduire la charge GPU tout en gardant une image détaillée. Le TAA (Temporal Anti-Aliasing) exploite plusieurs images successives et les vecteurs de mouvement pour lisser les bords et stabiliser le rendu, mais il peut introduire du flou ou des artefacts sur les fins détails. PSSR 2 (Sony) et FSR 4 (AMD) sont des techniques de reconstruction qui utilisent elles aussi des informations temporelles et spatiales, avec des approches et une qualité variables selon le contenu affiché. Le principe reste le même : économiser du calcul en rendu natif, puis « remonter » la définition pour viser une sortie 4K ou 1080p plus propre.

articles.txt:
As we previously reported, many PC gamers are frustrated by the lack of an official PC version of GTA 6 . Some have already stated that they intend to play an unofficial recompilation once it's ready – and that could happen sooner rather than later. The community-run website PortWatchVI , which tracks the development of unofficial PC ports, now monitors 39 different projects. According to the website's scoring system, the leading project, known as CGBJ, has already reached 91.5% completion.

The 91.5% figure is not an average across all projects but refers specifically to the current frontrunner, CGBJ. Visual quality is reportedly largely on par with the console version, aside from minor rendering issues, while crashes are said to be infrequent. Community is thinking in days rather than months The rapid progress is fueling growing excitement within the community. According to comments on a since-deleted gameplay video of the CGBJ project posted on Reddit , GPU utilization was as low as 5%, while the CPU was under heavy load. This suggests that performance may currently be limited primarily by a CPU bottleneck, leaving considerable scope for improvements through further optimization. For now, however, that remains speculation. In any case, it will be interesting to see how the recompilation projects progress over the coming days.

articles.chapeau: Take-Two used a DMCA notice to remove Leonida, the GTA 6 PC port project, covering 1 repo and 2,900+ forks. What is confirmed and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. has shut down Leonida, an unofficial project that aimed to bring Grand Theft Auto VI to PC. The company, which owns Rockstar Games, sent GitHub a DMCA takedown request covering one repository and more than 2,900 forks, and GitHub removed the project after the complaint. Reports from Mashable, The Verge, Eurogamer, Nacionale, Metro.co.uk and NoobFeed, dated between November 24 and 26, 2026, describe the sequence.
This analysis takes a different angle than our first-day report on the Leonida DMCA action . Instead of retelling the headline, it asks what the notice says, why the fork count matters, how a takedown against a fork network works in general terms, and what PC players and developers should take from it. It also flags every claim that remains unconfirmed, because the rumor mill around this game has been loud all month.
The short version has three anchors. Take-Two says Leonida infringed its copyrighted works. No PC release date for GTA 6 has been confirmed. And nothing in the confirmed record shows the project produced a complete, playable PC port. Everything below builds on those three points.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with what the record supports. The project was called Leonida. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., the parent company of Rockstar Games, submitted a DMCA takedown request to GitHub. The request named ItsNotRexed’s GitHub repository and more than 2,900 forks attached to it. GitHub then removed the project following the complaint.
The project was described in coverage as an unofficial effort to run or bring Grand Theft Auto VI to PC. That wording matters. Reports describe an attempt, not a finished product. Nothing in the confirmed facts says a player could download Leonida and boot a stable game, and several outlets stopped short of claiming that.
Reports dated November 24 through 26, 2026 describe the takedown, which makes this a story that broke across a single news cycle. It moved fast because the game itself dominates gaming search right now, and PC players have spent weeks hunting for any sign of a port. A takedown against the most visible fan attempt answers one question and raises several others.
The notice identified its sender as the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games. That phrasing is worth a second look. The request came from the corporate parent’s enforcement group, not from a studio spokesperson, which tells you this is a routine legal workflow rather than a public relations gesture. Large publishers keep dedicated teams for this work, and notices like this one tend to go out quietly and in volume.
The core statement is short. Take-Two wrote: “We are writing to submit a takedown request regarding ItsNotRexed’s GitHub repository and the 2900+ forks attached to it that infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
Read it closely and two separate theories appear. The first says the repository itself infringes Take-Two’s copyrighted works. The second says it facilitates infringement of Grand Theft Auto VI by others. A rights holder can lean on either theory, and pairing them makes the notice harder to dodge on a technicality. Take-Two did not need to prove that Leonida distributed the game. It only needed to assert that the project helped others copy it.
A single repository is easy to remove. A fork network is the real enforcement problem. On GitHub, anyone can copy a public repository into their own account with one click, and each copy carries the full code and history. When a project goes viral, those copies multiply within hours, which is exactly the dynamic that makes a 2,900-plus fork count so telling.
By naming the forks in the same notice, Take-Two avoided a slow game of whack-a-mole. Filing separate complaints against thousands of accounts would take weeks. A single notice that references the repository and its attached forks compresses that work into one step. For a publisher with a high-value launch to protect, the economics are obvious.

articles.t: Cyberleek released the missing executable for its leaked 209GB GTA 6 Xbox build, and an open source project says the game now boots on Windows but runs at about 1 frame per second in the world, not playable - Make Tech Easier
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek released the main executable for its leaked 209GB GTA 6 Xbox build on 23 November, and the open source VIctory project says the game boots on Windows but runs at about 1 frame per second in the world, not playable.
articles.txt:
Practical fixes for the tech you already own. Free, a few times a week.
The main executable for the leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 began circulating on 23 November 2026, according to TalkEsport . XDA Developers reported that the executable had become public and completed the Xbox build. Cyberleek put the size of the rest of that build at around 209GB, according to TalkEsport. The open source project VIctory says in its GitHub README that the game boots on a Windows PC and reaches the prologue. The project reports about 1 frame per second in the game world and describes the game as unplayable at that frame rate.
PC Gamer reported that Cyberleek had released a near-complete Xbox build the previous week but had held back the main executable. Cyberleek had said it would release the file when its crypto coin reached a $15 million market cap or on 23 November, whichever came first. TalkEsport reported that the rest of the build had been online since 19 November. According to accounts tracking the release, which TalkEsport cited, the executable began circulating shortly before 3pm UTC on 23 November.
Cyberleek called the release “an early Christmas gift” for followers, according to PC Gamer. The outlet reported that Cyberleek framed the release as a handover to people trying to get the game running on PC. Cyberleek added, “The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects.” PC Gamer’s Andy Chalk wrote that Cyberleek appeared to have followed through on the release and said he had not verified whether the executable was genuine.
XDA identified Cyberleek as the same individual or group behind GTA 6 leaks from earlier in the year. It also reported that Cyberleek had published SHA-256 hashes for both the executable and its ZIP archive. XDA’s report appeared on 23 November, the day the executable began circulating, and the outlet updated it on 24 November.
TalkEsport reported that clips showed the leaked build reaching its opening settings screens on PC within hours of the executable’s release. TalkEsport said none of the progress it covered had been independently verified.
VIctory’s GitHub repository was created at 21:47 UTC on 23 November 2026, according to GitHub’s records. The project uses the GPL-3.0 license. The repository was created the same day the executable began circulating, according to the dates reported by GitHub and TalkEsport. In a status update dated 25 November 2026, the README says the title boots, the menus run at 30 fps and the game loads its world. The README also says it plays the intro cutscene and reaches the prologue.
The menus and the world run at different speeds in VIctory’s account. The README says, “Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the world.” The project reports testing on one machine running Windows 11 and equipped with an AMD RX 6700 XT graphics card with 12 GB of memory. The frame rates and milestones in the README describe that test. The README names the frame rate as what keeps the game from being playable. It also warns that entering the world hung the GPU in earlier builds and that a run can still end on a GPU fault.
XDA’s 24 November update named VIctory among the unofficial GTA 6 PC projects tracked by a site called PortWatch VI, and said that site probably isn’t an entirely accurate picture of the projects’ status. The same update reported, according to Leonida developer NotRexed, that the Leonida project was removed from GitHub after a DMCA notice .
PC Gamer warned that files from strangers can contain malware. TalkEsport reported that security firms were warning about fake GTA 6 PC downloads spreading malware. Make Tech Easier reported that a GTA 6 PC port scam kit was being offered on the dark web for $200 in Bitcoin or Tether, citing NordVPN.
As of TalkEsport’s report, Rockstar Games had yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6. The outlet reported that neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two Interactive had made a public comment about the leak. VIctory’s README says the game reached the prologue in its Windows test. The project’s account says the game was unplayable because of the frame rate once it loaded the world.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC Leak: 1 Xbox Build, 0 Official PC Dates
articles.chapeau: A leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 has PC gamers hopeful, but Rockstar has announced no GTA 6 PC version, date or specs. Here is the catch.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A new GTA 6 leak is handing PC gamers something they have wanted since Rockstar Games shipped Grand Theft Auto VI on consoles: a possible way in. The catch is big. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, and Grand Theft Auto VI is not officially available on PC, according to Polygon’s coverage of the story.
The leaker known as Cyberleek reportedly released an executable tied to a leaked Xbox build of the game, described as a November 2026 build. Our earlier report on the 57 MB executable leak covered the first wave of that drop and found no playable PC build. This analysis looks at what the leak means, what it does not prove, and where the hype is running ahead of the evidence.
The list of confirmed facts is short, so we keep it separate from the rumor pile. Anything not on that list gets labeled as unconfirmed, attributed to reports, or left out. If you came here for a PC release date, a price, or a spec sheet, the honest answer today is that none of them exist officially.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Reports say Cyberleek released an executable associated with a leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI. The build is described as dating from November 2026. Cyberleek reportedly wrote that “CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent.”
That one sentence is the only on-record statement from the leaker in the reporting we reviewed. It claims possession of a full build and says distribution happens by torrent. It does not say the build runs on a PC, and it does not say the files are complete in any way a normal player could use.
The game itself is developed by Rockstar Games and goes by both Grand Theft Auto VI and GTA 6. Both names show up in the coverage, and both refer to the same title. The Xbox label matters because the leaked build targets Microsoft’s console, not a PC storefront or a PlayStation release.
Polygon framed the episode around a simple tension. The leak looks like good news for people waiting on a GTA 6 PC release, yet it comes with a catch that the headline itself flags. We unpack both halves below, starting with why PC players care.
PC players have spent months watching console owners play. A leak involving an Xbox build feeds a hope that PC is a short technical step away. That hope is understandable. It is also, for now, a feeling rather than a finding.
In our analysis, the Xbox angle explains much of the excitement. Xbox consoles run on x86 processors and a graphics stack that sits close to what Windows PCs use. Enthusiasts have long watched Xbox builds for that reason, because they tend to be the nearest console relative of a PC version. That closeness is a reason for curiosity, not proof that a leaked build converts cleanly.
The second source of optimism is timing. A build dated November 2026 is recent, which suggests the files reflect the game close to its current state. Still, a recent date says nothing about whether the files are complete, stable, or runnable outside Microsoft’s hardware.
Some fans hope the leak will push Rockstar to move up an official PC release. That hope is on the unconfirmed list. Nothing in the reporting shows Rockstar changing any plan in response, and a company the size of Take-Two does not usually reshuffle a launch schedule because of a leak.
So the good news is narrow. The leak shows a build exists in the wild, and it gives PC gamers a fresh reason to ask Rockstar for a plan. That is all the evidence supports.
Rockstar Games has not officially announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI. Polygon and other outlets in the coverage agree on that point, and it anchors everything else. No release date, price, system requirements, performance targets, or official Rockstar statement on PC exists in the verified reporting.
The gap is not new. Our look at the March 2027 PC talk tracked a single leak with zero Rockstar confirmations. The pattern has repeated since: a claim surfaces, forums amplify it, and the publisher says nothing.
The reporting is blunt here. There is no official statement from Rockstar Games on PC availability in connection with this leak. Silence is not denial, and it is not a green light either. It means readers should treat every PC date and every PC spec in circulation as rumor.
That includes the Q1 2027 PC release window that some reports mention. Outlets cit

articles.t: GTA 6 After Launch: How Rockstar Keeps the Hype
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 after launch: Rockstar confirmed $79.99 and $99.99 editions plus a 34-track album, but no roadmap. Here is what is known and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI has been on sale for a week, and the conversation has already shifted from when it ships to what happens next. According to Creative Bloq , the real test of the game’s success is not the launch itself. The outlet’s framing is simple: now that the game is out, how does Rockstar keep up the hype? That question matters more than any opening-week headline, because a release date only sets the starting line for a long commercial race.
The facts on the table are narrow. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) announced that Grand Theft Auto VI became available on November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games said the game “is now available.” Beyond that, Rockstar has not detailed a post-launch roadmap, and our earlier launch coverage already flagged that PC remains undated. This analysis separates what the companies have confirmed from what observers expect, and it labels every forecast as opinion.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
A launch is an event. Success is a trend line. Publishers have understood that gap for years, yet it hits hardest with a title as large as Grand Theft Auto VI, where the marketing machine ran for a long stretch before release day. When a campaign peaks on the day of release, the next phase has to replace it with something that keeps players talking, buying and returning.
Creative Bloq’s argument rests on that logic. A record-sized opening can look impressive on a slide, but it says little about whether players stay engaged a month later, whether word of mouth stays positive, or whether new buyers arrive after the first wave of fans has finished. Those later signals decide how a game gets remembered. They also decide how much value Take-Two extracts from a single release over its life.
The timing adds pressure. The game reached stores on November 19, 2026, which puts it in the middle of the holiday shopping season. That gives Rockstar a built-in second wave of attention as gift buyers enter the market. It also means the studio competes for time and wallet share with every other holiday release, a factor we return to in the competitive section below.
Because the story invites speculation, it helps to pin down the verified record first. Take-Two’s announcement and related Rockstar materials establish a short list of facts. Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The standard edition costs $79.99. The Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. The ESRB rated the game M for Mature. The game is a single-player experience.
Distribution details are also on the record. Digital pre-orders could begin pre-loading on November 12, 2026. The physical version, which includes a download code inside the box, also became available on November 12, 2026. A separate product, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, carries 34 original tracks and is described as the official soundtrack from Atlantic Records.
Everything outside that table counts as unconfirmed for this article. That includes any content roadmap, any live-service plan, any multiplayer feature, and any specific method Rockstar will use to sustain interest. The company has said none of it in the sources available to us.
Creative Bloq, a design and creative-industry publication, put the idea in its headline: the measure of the game’s success will not be the launch. The framing treats the release as a milestone rather than a verdict. For a publication focused on creative work, that makes sense. Visual identity, trailers, key art and social campaigns drive attention before release, while the product itself has to carry attention afterward.
We cannot reproduce the full text of that piece here, and we do not claim to know every argument inside it. What we can say is that the headline’s thesis is an editorial position, not a measured result. Treat it as informed commentary. No sales ceiling, retention rate or review aggregate in the fact sheet proves or disproves it.
The thesis still holds up on its logic. A marketing push builds anticipation, and anticipation is a finite resource. After release, the audience splits into players who love the game and talk about it, players who finish it and move on, and buyers who wait for a discount. Each group needs a different reason to keep the title in the conversation. Rockstar’s job over the coming months is to serve all

articles.t: The state of GTA 6 on PC: Everything you need to know
articles.chapeau: The race to play GTA 6 on PC is moving by the hour, so here is where every fan port, project, and emulation attempt stands right now.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is undoubtedly the biggest game ever created, and some might argue it's the biggest entertainment project of all time. Rockstar has confirmed that GTA 6 made $3.79 billion on the first day of launch, shattering entertainment records. It was the most pre-ordered title on both the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and it even earned a spectacular Metacritic score of 99. However, one thing was missing from GTA 6's historic launch.
Rockstar's masterpiece launched on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but not on PC. That wasn't a surprise omission, but it's still a big chunk of the player base that missed out on experiencing GTA 6 at the same time as the rest of the world. We have come to expect this pattern from Rockstar, as GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 both launched on PC some time after their original console launches. Most likely, that is exactly what will happen with GTA 6. However, it looks like PC players aren't waiting around.
Popular Now: Rockstar is handing out 100 of these gorgeous limited-edition GTA 6 PS5 consoles, and you can't buy one What Rockstar has said so far First, we have to talk about what Rockstar has officially said. Surprisingly, Rockstar hasn't confirmed a PC version yet, and neither has Take-Two, its parent company. However, given the history of previous Rockstar launches, we can make an educated guess that an official PC version will eventually come out. The closest thing to a timeline is a GamesBeat report in which four industry sources said Rockstar is targeting the first quarter of 2027 for GTA 6 on PC. That was in October, and we haven't heard any new rumors since.
6 A car meet in Grand Theft Auto VI, which launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S without a confirmed PC version. VIEW GALLERY - 6 IMAGES Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said in November that Take-Two is beefing up its defenses against AI-assisted reverse engineering and unofficial PC ports, so they were definitely prepared for the onslaught. Shortly after GTA 6's November 19 launch, people started testing the waters, trying to port GTA 6 to PC themselves. Of course, nobody had any luck at first, but the breakthrough came via notorious leaker Cyberleek, who had been pestering Rockstar for months before launch.
On November 19, Cyberleek announced it had a full November 2026 Xbox build. The roughly 209 GB package was uploaded shortly after, but without the main executable. That part was locked behind a countdown, partly tied to a meme coin goal. Regardless of that attempt to pump up his meme coin, Cyberleek dropped the .exe on November 23, alongside a statement calling the whole thing a protest against subscriptions. At this point, it is important to remember this wasn't a PC build, but an Xbox Series X one. Getting the files and the executable did not mean you could just copy them to your PC, run the .exe, and jump into Leonida. It's not quite that simple.

GTA 6 à 120 FPS sur PS6 et Xbox Helix, un insider dévoile ses estimations
articles.chapeau: Bloqué à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series, GTA 6 rallume pourtant le débat performance avec une fuite ciblant la future PS6 et la Xbox Project Helix. Jusqu’où ces consoles next gen pourraient pousser le compteur d’images par seconde ?
articles.txt:
Bloqué à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series, GTA 6 rallume pourtant le débat performance avec une fuite ciblant la future PS6 et la Xbox Project Helix. Jusqu’où ces consoles next gen pourraient pousser le compteur d’images par seconde ?
Pour l’instant, les joueurs consoles vivent GTA 6 en 30 FPS fixes, que ce soit sur PS5 , PS5 Pro ou Xbox Series X|S . Aucun mode 40 ou 60 FPS n’est proposé, Rockstar Games assumant ce choix pour préserver la densité de l’open world et les effets de ray tracing.
Une nouvelle fuite relance pourtant l’espoir des amateurs de fluidité. Le leaker Moore’s Law Is Dead affirme que GTA 6 pourrait tourner en 60 FPS, voire viser un mode 120 FPS, sur la future PlayStation 6 et la Xbox Project Helix . De quoi faire rêver ceux qui jouent déjà sur des téléviseurs 120 Hz.
Sur les machines actuelles, les analyses de Digital Foundry parlent d’un rendu autour du 1440p à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series X , avec un avantage pour Xbox grâce au 120 Hz et au VRR. Un bug Quick Resume sur Xbox peut même pousser temporairement GTA 6 au delà de 40 FPS, mais en accélérant le jeu, ce qui le rend injouable.
C’est dans ce contexte que Moore’s Law Is Dead affirme que PS6 et Xbox Helix auront un GPU au niveau d’une GeForce RTX 5080 : dans sa vidéo, il parle d’« the equivalent of a 5080 for the GPU », citation rapportée par Notebookcheck. Selon lui, un 60 FPS stable serait réaliste, avec un mode 120 FPS pensé comme option performance, même si l’insider Kepler_L2 reste nettement plus prudent sur la PS6 .
D’après ces fuites , la PlayStation 6 viserait jusqu’à 40 Compute Units RDNA 5 . Moore’s Law Is Dead va jusqu’à dire que ce GPU pourrait dépasser une RTX 5080 en ray tracing et se rapprocher d’une Radeon RX 9070 XT en rasterisation, ce qui placerait une version next gen de GTA 6 bien au delà des consoles actuelles.
La Xbox Project Helix irait plus loin encore avec jusqu’à 56 Compute Units RDNA 5 , davantage de bande passante mémoire et un recours massif au FSR pour reconstruire une image 4K. Côté processeur, Helix passerait de 8 cœurs Zen 2 à jusqu’à 11 cœurs Zen 6 au delà de 4 GHz, de quoi gommer le goulot d’étranglement CPU qui empêche déjà aujourd’hui GTA 6 de grimper au dessus des 30 FPS.
Moore’s Law Is Dead évoque une mise en production de la PS6 au deuxième trimestre 2027, pour une sortie entre fin 2027 et début 2028. Xbox Helix viserait la même fenêtre , mais avec un positionnement bien plus haut de gamme, autour de 1 000 à 1 200 dollars, soit environ 950 à 1 150 € en Europe.
Dans ce scénario, un Grand Theft Auto VI « Enhanced » pour PS6 et Xbox Helix avec un mode 60 FPS paraît très probable, tandis qu’un mode 120 FPS resterait conditionné à des compromis sur la résolution et le ray tracing. Tant que Rockstar Games ne confirme rien, ces chiffres doivent être vus comme des objectifs ambitieux plutôt que comme une promesse ferme.
